mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate triggers a forward discounting effect on equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days by compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days by compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) signals weak labor demand, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in slack periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days by reducing investor confidence in economic recovery.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in slack periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
